I am 52 years old, and I have worked my 8 mu of flat land in Quzhou County since I was a young man. I finished middle school, so I can read seed labels and figure fertilizer rates well enough. My father taught me the wheat-maize rotation, and that is what I still do — it is what every household around here does, and the grain buyers and government subsidies make it a safe living.

It is now spring, and my winter wheat is already in the field. I sowed it last October after running the rotary tiller. I use luyuan502, an improved variety that performs reliably on our land. Right now the wheat is greening up, and my first job is to topdress it with urea and give it the first irrigation. I will irrigate three more times before early June, when I harvest. I also spray twice for aphids and other insects, once for weeds, and once for fusarium head blight — four pesticide passes in total. I expect about 1000 jin per mu, maybe a bit more if the weather cooperates.

As soon as the wheat comes off in June, I will plant summer maize. I buy denghai605 hybrid seed from the supply store every year; it is what everyone plants here because it yields well and stands up to our summers. I do not till for the maize — I sow directly into the wheat stubble to save diesel and time. I put down compound fertilizer at sowing and irrigate twice during the summer. The maize needs two insecticide sprays and one herbicide spray. I expect around 1100 jin per mu by October.

I thought about putting some land into cotton or vegetables, but cotton needs too much labor and pesticides, and vegetable prices jump around too much. At my age, I do not want to gamble or hire extra workers. The wheat-maize double crop uses my 8 mu twice a year, gives me steady grain income, and I can manage it almost entirely with my wife and occasional help from my nephew.
